text: @local/dsh-lean-mode 是面向 DSH 的工具呈现插件，通过 profile 层监听系统提示词装配，在指定的 Lean preset 会话中精简工具参数 schema，并可添加工具目录。它保留顶层参数契约、必填字段和嵌套结构，压缩过长描述，也支持按校验哈希匹配覆盖描述；需要补充整理的描述会记录到 pending 文件。适合挂载大量工具、希望减少提示词上下文的 DSH 用户。插件通过 bundle 同时声明 Lean 模式 preset；代码未声明 API 密钥或外部服务。

@local/dsh-lean-mode compacts DSH tool schemas in selected Lean sessions. It preserves required and nested parameters, shortens long descriptions, and can add a tool catalog. Hash-checked description overrides and a pending curation file are supported. The bundle declares the Lean preset.
工具太多占满上下文，想让 DSH 更精简地展示工具定义。
能不能在保留参数结构的同时缩短工具 schema？
我想只在某个会话 preset 下启用精简工具描述。
@local/dsh-lean-mode 的功能「精简工具 schema」：在匹配的 preset 会话中投影工具参数，保留顶层键、必填项和嵌套结构。系统提示词装配时自动触发，输出精简后的工具定义。
@local/dsh-lean-mode 的功能「工具描述压缩与目录」：装配时压缩长描述，并可在提示词中列出工具目录；配置还可启用经过哈希校验的描述覆盖及待整理清单。

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · The problem：Tool schemas are sent on **every** request. In a deployment with hundreds of MCP tools they dominate the context:

| Deployment | Tools | Tool schemas | Share of the first request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default `standard` preset (measured on a real deployment) | **84** | **89 KB** | **~22,300 of 36,264 tokens — 61.6%** |
| All MCP tools mounted | **731** | **988 KB** | **~275,000 tokens — 27.5% of a 1M window** |

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · The problem：Most of that is JSON-Schema punctuation the model rarely needs: nested descriptions, deep objects, defaults. The **names** and the **top-level contract** are what make a call possible.

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Why the envelope must survive：In a real catalogue **64% of tools take a single required wrapper key** (commonly `params`). Collapse the schema to an open `{type:'object'}` and the model flattens the arguments, so every call is rejected:

| Channel shape | Calls that actually execute |
|---|---|
| Open skeleton `additionalProperties: true`
 | **1.7%** |
| **Top-level contract kept** | **95.0%** |

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Measured effect：Same model, same 199-task set, same catalogue:

| Tools | Baseline (full schemas) | **lean** | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26 | ~5,340 tok | ~2,385 tok | 0.45 |
| **84** (a real deployment's default preset) | ~22,300 tok | **~9,400 tok** | **0.42** |
| **731** (every MCP tool) | **~275,000 tok** | **~68,000 tok** | ★ **0.247** |

End-to-end callability (tool name in the catalogue **and** the emitted arguments satisfy the real schema):

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Measured effect：| Presentation | End-to-end |
|---|---|
| Full JSON Schema | 95.0% |
| **lean** | **89.9%** |
| Open skeleton only | 1.7% |

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Install：**From GitHub** (verified end to end: installed this way, the mode appears in the UI preset menu and takes effect)

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:q862877400-ux/dsh-lean-mode
```

**From a local checkout**

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add <path to this directory>
```

**Uninstall**

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @local/dsh-lean-mode
```

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Install：The bundle carries both the plugin row and a **Lean mode** preset declaration, so once installed the mode appears in the UI's preset menu; removing the bundle removes both.

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `presets` | `undefined` | Preset ids this applies to. Omit to apply to **every** session. |
| `shape` | `true` | Project parameters to the top-level contract. |
| `catalog` | `true` | Append the `tools:catalog` section. |

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Limitations：- ★ **All figures were measured on one local deployment** (731-tool catalogue unioned from real sessions; 199 tasks; a single model). Ratios will differ elsewhere — **re-measure before relying on them**.
- ★ Callability is judged as **"the emitted call is valid against the real schema"**, not "the tool succeeded on a machine".
- ★ End-to-end accuracy (89.9% vs 95.0%) is a **single-run** figure on that task set.
- ★ The catalogue **repeats each tool's one-line purpose**, so the win grows with the **size of the parameters**, not merely the count of tools.

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Writing tool definitions：**The normative source for model-facing tool definitions (name / description / parameter schema) is DSH's own [`agent-experience`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) skill** — `app/source/.agents/skills/agent-experience/SKILL.md`. This plugin does not define a competing standard.

Use the docs below only for the **lean presentation layer** on top of it:

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Writing tool definitions：| Doc | Read it when |

| [`docs/tool-description-style.md`](docs/tool-description-style.md) | Writing descriptions; §10 covers the one real conflict with `agent-experience` |
| [`docs/authoring-mcp-tools.md`](docs/authoring-mcp-tools.md) | Authoring MCP tools for DSH under lean |
| [`docs/when-to-use.md`](docs/when-to-use.md) | Deciding which of the three presentation tiers to use |
| [`docs/core-requirement.md`](docs/core-requirement.md) | Why the plugin exists |
| [`skills/lean-tool-presentation/SKILL.md`](skills/lean-tool-presentation/SKILL.md) | Agent-facing summary of all of the above |

@local/dsh-lean-mode README · Writing tool definitions：**Check your tools mechanically:** `node tools/lean-lint.mjs tools.json` — reports real information loss, the pending-curation list, and the byte ledger.
